docs.title: What Melo is
docs.text:
Melo is a Discord bot for moderation, community features, economy, logging, and server setup. It is slash-command only, so people can discover commands in Discord and only see commands they can use.

65 public commands 9 command categories 1 unified setup flow 0 prefix commands

docs.title: What you can do with Melo
docs.text:
⚙️ Set up a server

Run the setup wizard, adjust settings, and save a config backup before major changes.

🛡️ Moderate with structure

Use warnings, timeouts, bans, case history, and Discord AutoMod with clear logs.

🎉 Keep people engaged

Run polls, giveaways, and thanks posts with options like anonymous votes and timed endings.

💰 Run an economy loop

Use wallets, banks, transfers, rewards, games, and leaderboards.

docs.title: Fast path
docs.text:
1. Open Getting Started and invite Melo through Discord’s OAuth2 flow.
  2. Run the setup wizard with /setup start.
  3. Use /help in Discord to browse every public command category.
  4. Move straight to the Command Reference if you already know what you need.

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text: This guide shows how to invite Melo, give the right permissions, and finish first-time setup.

docs.title: 1. Invite Melo
docs.text:
Use Discord’s OAuth2 URL generator in the Developer Portal to create an invite for Melo’s bot application.

Invite links should include these scopes:

  • bot
  • applications.commands

Tip

Melo is slash-command only, so the invite link only needs the bot and applications.commands scopes.

Invite checklistRecommended permissions
  • Create or open the bot application in Discord’s Developer Portal.
  • Generate an OAuth2 URL with the correct scopes.
  • Give the bot only the permissions your server actually needs.
  • Add Melo to a test server first if you want to validate setup before rolling it out widely.
Permission Why it matters View Channels Lets Melo see the channels where commands are used Send Messages Lets Melo respond to slash commands Embed Links Renders rich responses correctly Read Message History Helps with moderation, logging, and context-sensitive commands Manage Messages Needed for cleanup and moderation actions Moderate Members Required for timeouts and related moderation actions Kick Members / Ban Members Required for enforcement commands Manage Roles Needed if you want the setup wizard to create role templates

docs.title: 2. Configure the Bot
docs.text:
Once Melo is in your server, run the setup wizard in a server where you have the required permissions. The /setup command is owner-only:

/setup start roles:Yes
/setup status
/setup reset

/setup start creates the guild record and can optionally create manager, admin, and moderator roles for your server.

roles:Yes creates the recommended role set. Choose roles:No if you want to manage roles yourself.

/setup status shows the current onboarding progress, and /setup reset clears the saved progress so you can start over.

First-run behavior

The wizard writes the guild record to the database as it progresses. If you reset the setup, you are only clearing the onboarding state, not deleting every other server setting.

docs.title: What the wizard creates
docs.text:
The setup flow can create a recommended role template for:

  • Manager
  • Admin
  • Moderator

It also records onboarding progress so /setup status can tell you exactly where the server is in the process.

docs.title: 3. Verify Everything Works
docs.text:
Run /ping to confirm Melo is online and responding:

/ping

You should see a response like:

🏓 Pong! Latency: 42 ms

docs.title: Next Steps
docs.text:
• Browse the Command Reference to see every public command category.
  • Join the Support Server if you need help.
  • Read the Permissions Guide if you want to understand who can use each command family.

docs.title: Commands Overview
docs.text:
Melo uses Discord’s native slash commands. Start typing / in any channel where Melo has access to see the autocomplete list.

This page lists public commands only.

docs.title: Channels
docs.text: The Channels category helps you control message pace and temporary voice access. These commands are usually used by moderators or admins.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text: Command What it does Access /slowmode Sets slowmode in the current channel or a target channel Moderators /tempvc Registers a voice channel as a temporary voice spawn point Administrators

docs.title: /slowmode
docs.text:
/slowmode accepts a duration such as 5s, 5m, 5h, or 5d. You can also disable slowmode with 0 or off.

/slowmode time:5m
/slowmode time:0
/slowmode time:10s channel:#announcements

docs.title: Good uses
docs.text:
• Slow down fast-moving announcement channels.
  • Cool off heated discussion without locking a channel.
  • Apply temporary rate limits during events or raids.

docs.title: /tempvc
docs.text:
/tempvc set-channel stores the voice channel that users should join to create temporary voice channels.

/tempvc set-channel channel:#join-to-create

docs.title: Good uses
docs.text:
• Create self-serve voice rooms for gaming or events.
  • Keep your channel list tidy by removing empty temporary rooms automatically.

Practical advice

Temporary voice channels work best when the spawn channel is easy to find, with a clear name like Join to Create.

docs.title: Community
docs.text: Community commands help you drive activity with polls, giveaways, and thanks posts.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text: Command What it does Access /poll Creates and manages polls Public /giveaway Starts, ends, or rerolls giveaways Moderators / admins /thanks Sends reputation-based thanks to another member Public

docs.title: Polls
docs.text:
/poll supports two formats:

  • create for multi-option polls with up to five choices
  • yesno for a simple yes/no choice

Useful options include:

  • duration for scheduled endings such as 30m, 1h, or 1d
  • anonymous to hide voter identities
  • multi_select to allow more than one answer
  • thread to create a discussion thread beside the poll
/poll create question:Best game night? option1:Valorant option2:Minecraft option3:Jackbox duration:1d thread:true
/poll yesno question:Should we run an event tonight? duration:6h anonymous:true

docs.title: Results and endings
docs.text:
• /poll results message_id:<id> shows live results privately.
  • /poll end message_id:<id> ends a poll early and displays the final outcome.
  • The original poll creator or a moderator can end a live poll.

Premium duration caps

Poll duration limits depend on whether the server has Melo Premium enabled. Free servers have shorter caps than premium servers.

docs.title: Giveaways
docs.text:
/giveaway start creates a reaction-based giveaway and records the end time.

/giveaway start prize:Nitro duration:1d winners:1
/giveaway end message_id:<id>
/giveaway reroll message_id:<id>

docs.title: Good uses
docs.text:
• Run event prizes with a fixed end time.
  • End a giveaway early if the schedule changes.
  • Reroll winners after the original giveaway finishes.

docs.title: Thanks
docs.text: /thanks adds to the guild reputation system and keeps a running count of who has given and received thanks.

docs.title: Behaviour to know
docs.text:
• You cannot thank yourself.
  • You cannot target bots.
  • The command enforces rate limits so users cannot spam reputation changes.
/thanks user:@helper reason:Helped with the setup

docs.title: Config
docs.text: The Config category covers setup, language, server settings, and backup/restore. Use this category when adding Melo to a new server or recovering from config mistakes.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text: Command What it does Access /setup Runs the onboarding wizard Server owner only /settings Opens the interactive settings panel Administrators / authorised users /language Changes the server locale Server managers /config Creates, lists, or restores config snapshots Server managers

docs.title: /setup
docs.text:
The setup wizard creates the guild record, tracks onboarding progress, and can optionally create a recommended role template.

/setup start roles:Yes
/setup status
/setup reset

docs.title: Role template
docs.text:
If you choose roles:Yes, Melo can create:

  • Manager
  • Admin
  • Moderator

Those roles are then saved into the guild settings so later moderation and setup tooling can reference them.

docs.title: /settings
docs.text:
/settings opens an interactive panel with configuration groups for:

  • modules
  • permissions

The panel is designed for admins or explicitly authorised roles and users. It is ephemeral, so it stays out of public channels.

docs.title: /language
docs.text:
/language switches the guild locale using one of the supported language choices.

/language locale:en
/language locale:de

docs.title: /config
docs.text: The config command works with snapshots. You can save and restore your server's core configuration state.

docs.title: What gets captured
docs.text:
• Locale and timezone
  • Manager, admin, and moderator role IDs
  • Automod status
  • Premium flags
  • Logging channels
  • Temporary voice channel settings

docs.title: Usage examples
docs.text:
/config backup
/config list
/config restore index:1

Restores overwrite live configuration

Restoring a snapshot updates the live guild record. Treat it as a recovery tool, not a casual toggle.

docs.title: Economy
docs.text: Economy is Melo’s largest public command category. It covers wallet and bank balances, transfers, daily/weekly rewards, games, progression, and manager tools.

docs.title: Commands at a glance
docs.text: Command What it does Access /balance Shows a user’s wallet balance Public /bank Opens or checks bank functionality Public /daily Claims the daily reward Public /weekly Claims the weekly reward Public /work Earns currency through work Public /give Gives money directly to another user Public /transfer Transfers bank funds to another user Public /leaderboard Shows the top users by wallet, bank, or total value Public /profile Shows an economy profile Public /quests Reviews quest progress Public /wheel Spins the reward wheel Public /blackjack Plays blackjack Public /roulette Plays roulette Public /slots Plays slots Public /crime Attempts a crime action Public /rob Attempts to rob another user Public /business Manages or views business progress Public /crypto Views crypto-related status Public /add Adds currency to a wallet or bank Managers / admins / owner / economy manager /take Removes currency from a wallet or bank Managers / admins / owner / economy manager

docs.title: Core wallet and bank flow
docs.text:
The basic loop is:

  1. Check your balance with /balance.
  2. Claim rewards with /daily, /weekly, or /work.
  3. Move currency around with /give or /transfer.
  4. Use /bank and /profile when you want a fuller view of the account.

docs.title: Important differences
docs.text:
• /give moves wallet currency between users.
  • /transfer moves bank currency, and both users need bank accounts.
  • /add and /take are administrative economy actions. They require one of: Manage Server, Administrator, server owner, or the configured economy manager role.

docs.title: Rewards and progression
docs.text:
/daily uses a 24-hour cooldown, and premium users can receive a bonus based on guild configuration.

/daily
/weekly
/work
/quests
/wheel

docs.title: Games and risk
docs.text:
Melo includes both low-stakes and high-stakes ways to engage with the economy:

  • /blackjack
  • /roulette
  • /slots
  • /crime
  • /rob
  • /business
  • /crypto

Account safety

Commands that move money between users include safeguards like bot checks, self-target checks, and insufficient-funds checks.

docs.title: Leaderboards
docs.text:
Use /leaderboard to compare wallet, bank, or total wealth across the server.

/leaderboard type:Wallet
/leaderboard type:bank
/leaderboard type:total

If you are setting up a new economy

Decide early whether your server should be casual or tightly controlled. Reward amounts and pacing are easier to tune before users build large balances.

docs.title: Fun
docs.text: The Fun category is lightweight. These commands are good for quick reactions and casual chat activity.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text: Command What it does /8ball Ask the magic 8-ball a question /advice Get a random piece of advice /cat Fetch a cat image /coinflip Flip a coin /dadjoke Show a dad joke /dog Fetch a dog image /fact Get a random fact /joke Show a joke /pokemon Fetch Pokémon-related content /rps Play rock-paper-scissors /urban Look up an Urban Dictionary definition

docs.title: How to use the category well
docs.text:
• Use /8ball and /coinflip when you want a quick decision without adding noise.
  • Use /cat and /dog when you want a reaction image instead of another text reply.
  • Use /rps when you want a self-contained mini-game.
  • Use /urban carefully if your community prefers lighter or filtered language.

No setup required

Fun commands need little setup. If one is unavailable, the cause is usually permissions or a wider bot issue.

docs.title: Logging
docs.text: Melo's logging system uses one public command to control whether logging is enabled, where logs are sent, and which event families are active.

docs.title: Command
docs.text: Command What it does Access /logging Configures the audit logging system Administrators

docs.title: Subcommands
docs.text: Subcommand What it does enable Turns logging on for the server disable Turns logging off for the server setchannel Chooses the log channel and log family toggle Enables or disables an event type status Shows the current logging configuration

docs.title: Channels
docs.text:
/logging setchannel supports these families:

  • main
  • messages
  • members
  • voice
  • roles
  • channels
  • moderation
/logging setchannel channel:#audit-logs type:main
/logging setchannel channel:#member-logs type:members
/logging setchannel channel:#mod-logs type:moderation

docs.title: Events
docs.text: The command can toggle individual event types for message, member, voice, and moderation activity.

docs.title: Message events
docs.text:
• message delete
  • message edit
  • message bulk delete

docs.title: Member events
docs.text:
• member join
  • member leave
  • member ban
  • member unban
  • member roles
  • member nickname

docs.title: Voice events
docs.text:
• voice join
  • voice leave
  • voice switch

docs.title: Moderation events
docs.text:
• mod ban
  • mod kick
  • mod mute
  • mod unmute
  • mod warn
  • mod unban

docs.title: Best practice
docs.text:
Keep one main logging channel and only split out the families you actually need. That keeps the audit trail readable and prevents low-value logs from burying important events.

Start with status

If logging feels confusing, open with /logging status first. It shows what is currently enabled before you change anything.

docs.title: Moderation
docs.text: The Moderation category covers enforcement actions, case tracking, automod setup, and nickname control.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text: Command What it does Access /automod Creates native Discord AutoMod rules Administrators /ban Bans a user, optionally for a duration Moderators /case Inspects a moderation case Moderators /history Views a member’s moderation history Moderators /kick Kicks a member Moderators /mute Times out a member Moderators /setnick Changes a member’s nickname Moderators /unban Removes a ban Moderators /unmute Removes a timeout Moderators /warn Issues a warning Moderators

docs.title: Ban and timeout flow
docs.text:
/ban supports a duration, so you can use it for temporary or permanent enforcement.

/ban user:@user reason:Spam duration:1d
/ban user:@user reason:Severe violation confirm_permanent:true
/mute user:@user duration:30m reason:Cooldown

docs.title: Important details
docs.text:
• Permanent bans require explicit confirmation.
  • Time-based bans accept compact durations such as 1d, 2h, or 30m.
  • The bot checks that it can actually act on the target before executing the action.

docs.title: Warnings and case tracking
docs.text:
/warn creates a moderation case and pushes the action into the logging pipeline when configured.

Use /case and /history when you need context on what happened before.

docs.title: AutoMod
docs.text:
/automod creates Discord native AutoMod rules for:

  • flagged words
  • invite links
  • spam
  • mention spam
  • custom keywords

docs.title: What to know
docs.text:
• Flagged-word rules can use the Discord preset list.
  • Mention spam requires a threshold.
  • Invite and keyword rules are capped by Discord’s rule limits.

docs.title: Moderation philosophy
docs.text:
Melo moderation works best when your team follows a consistent flow:

  1. Warn first where possible.
  2. Escalate to timeouts or bans when needed.
  3. Log the reason every time.
  4. Review cases later through /case or /history.

Use the minimum force that solves the problem

The bot supports strong enforcement actions, but the cleanest moderation history comes from using the lightest action that still protects the server.

docs.title: Roles
docs.text: The Roles category is small but useful. It helps you inspect role details quickly without opening Discord's role editor.

docs.title: Command
docs.text: Command What it does Access /roleinfo Shows role metadata, stats, and key permissions Public

docs.title: What you get
docs.text:
/roleinfo surfaces:

  • name
  • ID
  • colour
  • creation date
  • member count
  • position
  • mentionable state
  • hoist state
  • managed state
  • key permissions
/roleinfo role:@Moderators

docs.title: When it is useful
docs.text:
• Audit a role before using it in setup or permission panels.
  • Confirm whether a role is mentionable or hoisted.
  • Compare the role’s key permissions to the expectations of your moderation setup.

docs.title: Utility
docs.text: Utility commands are the general-purpose tools most people use first. They cover bot status, member lookups, permission checks, embeds, invites, and more.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text: Command What it does Access /avatar Shows a user’s avatar Public /embed Builds or sends a custom embed Administrators /emoji Inspects or copies an emoji Public /help Browses commands or looks up one command Public /info Shows bot information Public /invite Displays the bot invite link Public /membercount Shows member counts Public /permissions Simulates whether a user or role can run a command Managers /ping Checks latency Public /server Shows server information Public /support Displays support links Public /uptime Shows bot uptime Public /whois Shows a member profile Public

docs.title: Recommended first commands
docs.text:
If you are new to Melo, start with these:

  1. /help to browse the command tree.
  2. /ping to confirm the bot is responsive.
  3. /info to confirm the bot version and uptime.
  4. /server to inspect the guild overview.

docs.title: Member lookups
docs.text:
/whois and /avatar are useful for moderation reviews and identity checks.

/whois user:@member
/avatar

/avatar currently returns your own avatar.

docs.title: /whois highlights
docs.text:
• joined server and Discord dates
  • reputation counters
  • roles
  • badges and notable flags
  • key permissions

docs.title: Diagnostics
docs.text:
/permissions is especially useful when a command seems missing or gated. It can simulate whether a user or role would pass Melo’s access checks for a specific command.

/permissions check command:ban user:@moderator
/permissions check command:logging role:@Admins

docs.title: Sharing and support
docs.text:
• /invite returns the bot invite link.
  • /support returns the support server link.
  • /embed helps you produce structured announcements or rich messages.

Use /help early

/help is the quickest way to confirm Melo loaded correctly after setup or deployment.

docs.title: Permissions Guide
docs.text: Melo does not use one flat permission model. Access depends on command type, your guild role setup, and Discord permissions.

docs.title: Main access layers
docs.text: Layer What it means Server owner Highest access level for setup and server-wide configuration Server manager Used by many configuration and economy-admin actions Server admin Used for settings, logging, automod, and strong moderation actions Server moderator Used for routine moderation commands Authorised settings roles and users Explicitly allowed to open /settings

docs.title: Common examples
docs.text:
• /setup is owner-only.
  • /settings checks for administrator access, server ownership, authorised roles, or authorised users.
  • /logging is for administrators.
  • Moderation commands use the moderator layer.
  • Economy admin commands like /add and /take are limited to economy managers, server managers, admins, or owners.

docs.title: How to check access
docs.text:
Use the permissions simulator when you are not sure why something is unavailable.

/permissions check command:ban user:@Moderator
/permissions check command:logging role:@Admins

docs.title: What the simulator shows
docs.text:
• which access checks passed
  • which access checks failed
  • whether the command is runnable for the selected user or role

docs.title: Configuring settings access
docs.text:
The settings panel can be opened by administrators, the server owner, authorised roles, or authorised users. That lets you delegate configuration work without handing over the entire server.

Keep access intentional

A clean setup is usually one moderation role, one configuration role, and one or two trusted users for /settings instead of giving everyone admin.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: This guide covers common setup and runtime issues in Melo.

docs.title: Commands are missing
docs.text:
If slash commands do not appear in Discord:

  1. Confirm the bot was invited with the applications.commands scope.
  2. Run npm run register in the bot repo if you are managing the deployment yourself.
  3. Wait for Discord’s global command cache if you recently changed command definitions.

docs.title: The bot does not respond
docs.text:
Check the following in order:

  • the bot token is configured correctly
  • the bot is online in the server
  • Melo has permission to view and send messages in the target channel
  • the channel is not blocked by your server’s own moderation rules

docs.title: Setup is stuck or incomplete
docs.text:
Use the setup commands in this order:

/setup status
/setup start roles:Yes
/setup reset

If the setup wizard created a partially configured state, reset it and start again from the server owner account.

docs.title: Logging looks empty
docs.text:
If /logging status shows disabled channels or event families, check:

  • whether logging is enabled at all
  • whether the correct channel family is selected
  • whether Discord permissions allow Melo to post in the target channel

docs.title: Economy data looks wrong
docs.text:
The economy system depends on the database. If balances, rewards, or profiles look stale:

  • confirm the database connection is healthy
  • verify the economy tables exist
  • retry the command after the database has finished syncing

docs.title: Temporary voice channels are not spawning
docs.text:
Confirm that:

  • /tempvc set-channel was pointed at a voice channel
  • the bot can manage channels in that category
  • the spawn channel is still the intended one

When in doubt, start small

Most Melo issues are easier to diagnose when you test one command family at a time instead of changing setup, logging, moderation, and economy at once.
